correctness.rationale: At a random pair the exact mean increment is \((2\mu/N)\tanh((\ell_j-\ell_i)/2)(x_j-x_i)\) plus selected-pair Gaussian noise. Exact orthogonal projection yields contraction \(a=1-4\mu(1-\mu)/(N-1)\), stationary centered second moment \((N-1)^2/[2N\mu(1-\mu)]\) and pair squared-difference mean \((N-1)/[N\mu(1-\mu)]\). Small-noise fourth-moment localization implies confidence interruptions vanish on each finite accelerated horizon; conditional quadratic observable martingale averaging and Gaussian functional CLT prove the stated diffusion. The invariant density follows from the zero-current ODE under integrability. Proof explicitly excludes stationary-law interchange. The exact-rational checker independently replays 45 finite \((N,\mu)\) identities.

value.rationale: The finite-N correction changes the effective Gibbs exponent, hence quantitative mean opinion selection and utility well weights, for natural small populations. For \(N=2\), \(\mu=1/2\) and \(U(x)=(1+x^2)^{-1}\), the corrected exponent is 2 rather than the source leading-N exponent 4. The result is not just the pair-count replacement: proving the exact limit requires control of stochastic fast disagreements, confidence cutoff and joint slow-fast averaging. It directly improves a documented approximation of the newly introduced model and marks the rigorous stationary interpretation boundary.
